name.description: Name of the workflow created by this spec from the {@link #createWorkflow} API.

initialDataCleanupSpec.description:
A {@link ReliabilityOrchestrator.ReliabilityRisk.Spec.DataCleanup} which will cleanup
data from the specified types before beginning the {@link Workflow}.

syntheticDataSpec.description:
A {@link ReliabilityOrchestrator.ReliabilityRisk.Spec.SyntheticData} which specifies
and controls the quantity of synthetic data that will be generated to setup the application
for use cases such as tutorials/demos/CI.

dataIntegrationSpec.description:
A {@link ReliabilityOrchestrator.ReliabilityRisk.Spec.DataIntegration} which specifies
and controls how data integration is done for the use case of `reliabilityRisk`. There
are two kinds of data ingestion, one that uses canonicals and another that relies
on asset hierarchy specification in an Excel spreadsheet. Specifications for both may
be set using this field.

calcFieldsRefreshSpec.description:
As part of setting up data, some stored calculated fields need to be refreshed
for proper functioning of the application. Use this field to specify a
{@link ReliabilityOrchestrator.ReliabilityRisk.Spec.RefreshCalcFields} to control
how the invalidation of stored calculated fields will occur in the application setup
process.

refreshNormalizationSpec.description:
As part of setting up data, time series data needs to be normalized
for proper functioning of the application. Use this field to specify a
{@link ReliabilityOrchestrator.ReliabilityRisk.Spec.RefreshNormalization} to control
how the time series normalization will occur in the application setup
process.

datasetPreparationSpec.description:
A critical step in deploying {@link ReliabilityRiskMlModel}s is to prepare clean
datasets that ensure the best possible model training outcomes. Use this field to
specify a {@link ReliabilityOrchestrator.ReliabilityRisk.Spec.DatasetPreparation} which
will control the quality of the datasets prepared and the distributed nature of the job
that will prepare these datasets.

modelTrainingSpec.description:
To deploy {@link ReliabilityRiskMlModel}s, they have to be trained. Use this field to
specify a {@link ReliabilityOrchestrator.ReliabilityRisk.Spec.ModelTraining} that controls
what {@link ReliabilityRiskMl.Pipeline}s will be trained and on what {@link ReliabilityAsset}s.

modelDeploymentSpec.description:
Use this field to specify what {@link ReliabilityAsset}s get `CHAMPION`
{@link ReliabilityRiskMlModel}s deployed against them for subsequent model inference.

finalDataCleanupSpec.description:
A {@link ReliabilityOrchestrator.ReliabilityRisk.Spec.DataCleanup} which will cleanup
data from the specified types after completion of the {@link Workflow}.

title:
A {@link Spec} object to control what portions of the overall, end to end {@link Workflow} to
run for the `reliabilityRisk` {@link MlProject}.
Depending on the fields set in this spec, the corresponding portion of the {@link Workflow}
will be run / not run.
The order to the sequential {@link Workflow} is as follows (each step is optionally specified by
the user as part of setting a value to that particular field):
1. Initial data cleanup (`initialDataCleanupSpec`)
2. Synthetic data generation (`syntheticDataSpec`)
3. Data integration (`dataIntegrationSpec`)
4. Refresh stored calculated fields (`calcFieldsRefreshSpec`)
5. Refresh normalization of time series (`refreshNormalizationSpec`)
6. Dataset preparation (`datasetPreparationSpec`)
7. Model training (`modelTrainingSpec`)
8. Model deployment (`modelDeploymentSpec`)
9. Model inference (`modelInferenceSpec`)
10. Final data cleanup (`finalDataCleanupSpec`)
For the {@link Workflow} that does get generated, refer to
{@link ReliabilityOrchestrator.ReliabilityRisk}.
name: ReliabilityOrchestrator.ReliabilityRisk.Spec
